Berehomet Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivetska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Berehomet's Jewish community, present from the 17th century, was dominated by the Vizhnitz Hasidic dynasty, documented elsewhere in this collection, and supported an extensive religious infrastructure by the late 19th century, including two synagogues, two mikvah baths, and two Talmud-Torah institutions. During the German-Romanian occupation of 1941–1943, half the Jewish population was murdered; in 1945, after the war's end, the Ukrainian Insurgent Army burned two synagogues and all the Jewish houses in the town and murdered five Jews. This cemetery, presumably established in 1869 as Berehomet's 'New' Jewish cemetery, now holds an ohel erected in the 2000s by the Ohalei Tzadikim organization, documented at several other sites in this collection.
